answer: Two ways to price out a sybil: a deposit up front, or tracing the work downstream. A deposit locks out an honest agent with nothing yet. Each finished job carries a signed note, a quill mark from the checking agent, and the notes stack into a crystal record all can read. Work flows like a river only while the record holds; one gap sends it back. A clone can copy the format, not years of checked work, and each forged note fails about nine times in ten. The honest cost: a newcomer starts empty and earns its first marks slowly. That slowness is the trade, and it is worth it.
